title: Subordinate Judicial Appointments
lead: The subordinate judiciary — the ==‘first line of defence’== — suffers ==23% vacancies== and accounts for ==87% of India's total pendency==.

items.title: Constitutional Framework
bullets: ==Art 233==: District Judges appointed by the ==Governor in consultation with the HC==
==Art 234==: subordinate judiciary by the Governor in consultation with ==HC and SPSC==
==Art 235==: ==control over the subordinate judiciary rests with the High Court==

items.title: How Recruitment Works
bullets: Each State has its ==own judicial service==; HC judges mostly come from it and from the State HC Bar
Split between the ==regular judicial service== and the ==higher judicial service==
District & Sessions Judges in the senior cadre; civil judges and magistrates in the lower
==Competitive exam by SPSC== in consultation with the HC — a ==3-year prior practice requirement== has recently been made mandatory
Bar members can enter the senior cadre directly with ==7+ years' practice== — District Judges need ==7 years== and are appointed by the Governor on the HC's recommendation

head: Case
Importance
rows: Norms for ==service conditions, fixed tenure, training==.
==Fixed calendar deadlines== for recruitment of judges.
==Delay in appointments violates access to justice==.

head: Body
Recommendation
rows: Creation of an ==All India Judicial Service (AIJS)==.
Fast-track courts, AIJS, improved conditions for judicial officers.
A ==common judicial service exam== and judicial academies.
Urgent steps to implement AIJS ==with consultation==.

items: ==Inconsistencies across States== in exams, syllabi and selection standards; no uniformity in eligibility and recruitment rules.
==Delays in filling vacancies== — ~==20–30% of sanctioned posts vacant== in many states.
==Political and executive interference== in some states.
==Poor service conditions, infrastructure and training==; no institutionalised judicial academy training across states.
==Training gaps== — newly recruited judges often under-prepared.

head: For AIJS
Against AIJS
rows: Solves vacancies and the talent crunch

blocks.text: A judiciary that fails at its lowest rung fractures the promise of justice at every level. Until appointments to the subordinate courts are made timely, transparently and uniformly, the lofty ideals of constitutional justice will remain paper-deep.
